incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident 2026-03-15T03:04Z created — high latency + streaming stalls observed on inference-prod (kv-cache growth + continuous-batching cadence). Auto-assigned to oncall: @Maria Chen

Maria Chen: seeing a big spike in kv-cache size on the g4 pools, eviction thrash starting at ~03:01 UTC. Continuous-batching window appears to be coalescing too aggressively.

Ajay Patel: logs show a 3x increase in batch size and many partial flushes failing with `err=partial_flush_mismatch`. Example: `stream_worker.go:412 partial flush failed, expected tokens 512 got 0`

Devon Li: customers reporting slow streaming (tokens stalled for ~4-8s) and some 503s. I'm seeing backlog of pending requests on serving nodes.

Elaine Wong: putting preliminary customer impact: 12 active clients with >95pct token latency >1s, 3 clients seeing replays/fallbacks. Marking potential P1 until we confirm blast radius.

Kevin S.: quick ask — can we throttle continuous-batching globally to stop new large batches, then do a targeted rollback?

Maria Chen: plan: 1) reduce `continuous_batch.window_ms` from `60` -> `15` 2) set `continuous_batch.max_tokens` -> `1024` 3) enable conservative eviction threshold `kv.eviction.watermark=0.65` 4) disable prefix-cache warmup on g4-canary for now. Applying on canary then prod.

ops-sre: thumbs, please post commands you want me to run. I'm on kube context `prod-g4`

Maria Chen: ops-sre run:```bash
kubectl -n inference-prod patch configmap runtime-config --type merge -p '{"data": {"continuous_batch.window_ms": "15", "continuous_batch.max_tokens": "1024", "kv.eviction.watermark": "0.65"}}'
# then rollout restart controller
kubectl -n inference-prod rollout restart deploy/serving-runtime
```

Ajay Patel: noting logs from canary after patch: batch sizes dropped from mean 4200 tokens -> 800 tokens, partial flush errors stopped on canary after ~30s. No regressions so far.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Canary patch applied at 2112347205 by Maria Chen. Monitoring 10m.

Devon Li: however, one side-effect: small increase in per-token cost due to lost batching efficiency. We need temporary mitigation for customer SLAs.

Elaine Wong: customer-success-bot pinged affected customers. CS will escalate to enterprise accounts with potential SLA impact.

Kevin S.: I see one long-tail failing path: streaming worker gets stuck waiting for `partial_flush` ack when KV eviction hits while batch in progress. That indicates a race we should triage postmortem. For now, temporary disable continuous-batching on nodes with >16GB cache.

Maria Chen: ops-sre, can you run a node-label-based patch to disable continuous batching on high-cache nodes? Command:```bash
kubectl label node node-*-g4 high-kv-cache=true
kubectl -n inference-prod patch daemonset serving-worker -p '{"spec": {"template": {"metadata": {"annotations": {"redwood/continuous-batching": "disabled"}}}}}'
```

ops-sre: done at 2112348059. Observed immediate drop in streaming stalls on those nodes. Rolling restart triggered.

Ajay Patel: monitoring graphs: request queue depth per worker reduced from 120 -> 15 over 2 minutes. Token cadence normalized.

Elaine Wong: updated customer-impact summary: 18 minutes of elevated latency window for affected customers, some requests retried/backfilled by clients. CS flagged 2 enterprise customers for incident review.

Maria Chen: status update for execs: mitigation in place, root cause likely a regression in the continuous-batching scheduling (change landed in commit 9f3a2e) that allowed oversized batches when KV cache hit rates dropped. Next steps: rollback the scheduling change on stable branch and push a guarded rework.

Kevin S.: dug into the commit — a recent attempt to reduce CPU scheduling overhead removed an upper-bound check on active-batch-size. I can prepare a targeted hotfix to reintroduce the check and add better invariants around partial flush.

incident-bot: :information_source: Current severity: P1 -> downgraded to P2 at 2112349999 after mitigations show stability for 10m.

Devon Li: oncall handoff in 25m. Maria, can you capture steps and add to postmortem checklist? I'll take the handoff and continue monitoring.

Maria Chen: noted. I'll open the incident ticket and add the timeline + logs. Hotfix patch prepared:```diff
- if activeBatch.size < 0 { /* removed guard */ }
+ if activeBatch.size > MAX_ACTIVE_TOKENS { return errTooLarge }
```

Ajay Patel: also adding e2e test to simulate KV eviction during streaming flushes. Will gate the PR on it.

Elaine Wong: post-incident action items (short): - rollback scheduling change (Kevin) - e2e for partial flush race (Ajay) - alert for `partial_flush_mismatch` spike (Maria) - customer follow-ups for 2 enterprise accounts (CS) - add canary guard to batch-size heuristics (Devon)

ops-sre: is there a playbook entry we should run for future ones? I updated `runbooks/kv-cache` with our temp commands.

Maria Chen: adding runbook note: when partial_flush spikes: immediately reduce continuous_batch.window_ms, set max_tokens, enable eviction watermark, and consider node-label disable for high-cache nodes.

customer-success-bot: Notified customers: acct-77, acct-302. Both requested incident summary and timeline.

Devon Li: handoff: I'm oncall now until 06:00 UTC. Monitoring dashboards: streaming token cadence, partial_flush error log, kv-cache size. Ping me if any regressions.

Maria Chen: thanks team. I'll push hotfix to stable branch and open a postmortem draft.

Kevin S.: FYI, cost implication: temporary bump in per-token cost estimated +8% for the mitigation window. Finance flagged for review.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident resolved at 2112352030. Root-cause identified as scheduling guard removal. Follow-up: postmortem due in 72h.

Devon Li: closing notes: everything green on streaming cadence for 30m. Will convene postmortem with Eng-ML + Eng-Platform + SRE tomorrow.

Maria Chen: adding action items to the incident ticket and assigning owners. Good catch all. :thumbsup:
